opportunities.title: The Ransomware Recovery Industry Is a Scam Wrapped in a Scam: MonsterCloud and the $19M 'Fake Decryption' Playbook
opportunities.why_now: Two simultaneous stories (SecurityWeek, Hacker News, The Register) detail how 'fixers' allegedly billed $11-19M while secretly paying ransoms or just lying about decryption.
opportunities.angle: Investigative explainer: name the pattern, map the fraud mechanics, give readers a checklist to vet an incident-response vendor before they wire money mid-crisis

opportunities.title: Someone Just Minted a Fake Google Cert by Hijacking .gh, .sl, and .as — Here's Why Your Browser Trusted It
opportunities.why_now: Multiple outlets (Register, Hacker News) confirm TLD-level hijacks were used to issue fraudulent certs for Google and other major orgs, a structural PKI failure.
opportunities.angle: Technical breakdown of the CA/TLD trust chain failure with a 'what this means for every org relying on domain validation' angle

opportunities.title: FortiBleed Isn't Done: Attackers Are Now Locking Admins Out of Their Own Fortinet Boxes
opportunities.why_now: FBI confirmed ongoing attacks and SecurityWeek reports a new lockout stage, showing the vuln has moved from 'patch now' to active exploitation chain with new impact.
opportunities.angle: Patch-cadence status update/timeline piece tracking FortiBleed from disclosure to lockout, with current IOCs and mitigation steps

opportunities.title: Oracle Health's Breach Tally Just Hit 20 Million — The Slow-Motion Disclosure Nobody's Watching
opportunities.why_now: The breach count climbing to nearly 20M signals either new discovery or a staged disclosure strategy worth scrutinizing against breach notification norms.

opportunities.title: They Said No to a Security Consultant. Ransomware Said Yes to Bankruptcy.
opportunities.why_now: The Register's story of a company going bust months after refusing to pay for security help is a perfect inevitable-breach cautionary tale with a clear moral.
opportunities.angle: Short, punchy post-mortem case study format — cost-of-skipping-security math, framed as a cautionary tale for SMBs
